# 01-upgrade-storage-sample: Upgrade the storage sample to .NET 10

Upgrade `storage-sample/Contoso.Documents.csproj` atomically from `net8.0` to `net10.0`, including stable .NET 10 SDK selection where appropriate. Replace the deprecated `WindowsAzure.Storage` 9.3.3 dependency with `Azure.Storage.Blobs`, `Azure.Storage.Queues`, `Azure.Storage.Files.Shares`, and `Azure.Data.Tables`, covering the blob, queue, file-share, table, credential, retry, paging, SAS, concurrency, and transactional-batch behavior used by the sample.

The package migration is the primary risk. The executor should use `StorageAccountFactory.cs`, `BlobRepository.cs`, `QueueRepository.cs`, `TableRepository.cs`, `DocumentEntity.cs`, and `FileShareRepository.cs` as research starting points, paying particular attention to queue encoding, missing table entities, SAS scope and expiry, continuation-based enumeration, optimistic concurrency, and fixed-size Azure Files uploads. Remove the vulnerable legacy dependency chain and the `NU1902`/`NU1903` suppressions, then validate the complete project in one bounded restore/build-and-fix pass. No generated test baseline is included because Test Coverage is set to Skip.

**Done when**: The project targets `net10.0`; a stable .NET 10 SDK is selected or explicitly documented; `WindowsAzure.Storage` and its vulnerable transitive dependency chain are absent; all four replacement Azure SDK packages are referenced; `NU1902` and `NU1903` are no longer suppressed; and a Release restore and build complete with zero warnings and zero errors. Any credential-dependent behavioral checks that cannot run locally are documented as deferred validation.

## Concrete migration research (2026-08-20)

- The machine has stable .NET 10 SDKs `10.0.203` and `10.0.303` installed (plus a `10.0.400-preview`); the project can target `net10.0` without adding a repository-wide `global.json` that might affect unrelated samples.
- Current stable package versions selected from the official NuGet/Azure SDK release listings are `Azure.Storage.Blobs` 12.29.1, `Azure.Storage.Queues` 12.27.1, `Azure.Storage.Files.Shares` 12.27.1, and `Azure.Data.Tables` 12.10.0.
- `StorageAccountFactory` must construct all four service clients from the same connection string or credential. Shared-key construction uses `StorageSharedKeyCredential`; SAS construction uses `AzureSasCredential` with explicit `https://{account}.{service}.core.windows.net` endpoints. Blob retries remain exponential (3-second delay, 4 retries, 5-minute network timeout), queue retries remain fixed (2-second delay, 3 retries), and queue message encoding must explicitly remain `None` to preserve legacy wire compatibility.
- Blob upload must send content type and both metadata values atomically through `BlobUploadOptions`. Listing becomes async pageable enumeration with metadata traits; append blobs retain create-on-first-use behavior without replacing an existing audit log; copy remains server-side; SAS generation retains read scope, the five-minute clock-skew start, and caller-supplied expiry; conditional overwrite maps the supplied string ETag to `BlobRequestConditions.IfMatch`, treating only HTTP 412 as a concurrency miss.
- Queue delayed send must preserve the legacy argument semantics (`timeToLive = 7 days`, caller delay as `visibilityTimeout`). Received messages are deleted with message ID plus pop receipt, batch receives retain a two-minute invisibility window, lease renewal uses the current pop receipt, and approximate length comes from `GetPropertiesAsync`.
- `DocumentEntity` will implement `ITableEntity` with `DateTimeOffset? Timestamp` and `Azure.ETag ETag`. Missing table entities must still return `null`, using `GetEntityIfExistsAsync`; typed and schema-less queries become `AsyncPageable` iteration; replace/merge modes remain distinct; batches remain chunks of at most 100 actions and must also respect the Azure Tables same-partition transaction requirement; optimistic replace treats only HTTP 412 as a false result.
- Azure Files upload requires a seekable length. To preserve stream support, a non-seekable input must first be buffered; then the file is created at the exact fixed size and uploaded by ranges. Listing filters directory entries with `IsDirectory`, and share quota comes from `ShareClient.GetPropertiesAsync().Value.QuotaInGB`.
- `Program` constructs repositories from Track 2 service clients without changing the no-credential exit path. Credential-dependent integration checks (real account/Azurite, SAS generation by credential type, queue interoperability, table transactions, and Azure Files range behavior) will be documented separately because no storage credentials are present in the repository.
